sourceFacts.fact: Bacteria ferment dietary sugars to acids that can remove enamel minerals.
Saliva minerals and fluoride support remineralisation of early noncavitated damage.
Net mineral loss over time can progress to a cavity.

labels: Caries develops when mineral loss exceeds repair
layout: Two separated horizontal lanes. TOP three cards1 to2 to3 linked by two coral arrows; BOTTOM two cards4 to5 linked by one teal arrow. Top shows sugar-square tokens, H+ coins, then mineral-square tokens leaving a plain rectangular inventory. Bottom shows water-drop and F tokens, then mineral squares added to a partially empty abstract inventory. Both inventories are tile racks, not enamel cross sections or tooth shapes. Large centre caption: Loss versus repair. Bottom note: Early mineral loss can be reversible; cavitation is later damage. No teeth, mouth, enamel layers, bacterial cells, acid dripping on a tooth, treatments or dose thresholds.
